svg.title: Destination choice, and what it does to the running cost
svg.desc: Three destination options for the same Function pipeline, ordered by cost. Azure Storage or Azure SQL is the cheapest: a few dollars a month, no capacity required, and Power BI Pro can import on a schedule, but you own the schema and the query layer. Fabric Lakehouse costs roughly zero incrementally if you already hold a capacity and lets you land a curated redacted schema, but it requires that capacity, and if you have one then Link to Fabric already gives you most of this with no code. Azure Data Explorer or Fabric Eventhouse is technically the best fit for the data shape, with native JSON parsing in KQL, update policies, retention policies and materialized views, but even the cheapest development tier is a standing hourly charge that dwarfs a couple of gigabytes a year. Below these, two costs are routinely left out of Function estimates: private endpoints are billed per endpoint, roughly twenty to twenty-five dollars a month for the three a hardened storage account typically needs, and Application Insights adds a few dollars a month. The conclusion is that the destination, not the code, decides whether the under ten dollars a month claim survives.
svg.text: The destination decides the bill, not the code
Same pipeline, same volume, three very different monthly invoices.
